{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3132f65b20e1e449b74e378bf63edf8d5a0600fdd762c8b37b9fc0214d832c00","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver programs, surcharges and the point system: DUI with a minor, driver improvement and probationary programs, defensive driving credits, violation surcharges, point values and interstate compacts","heading":"C — Driver programs, surcharges and points: DUI with a minor aboard, the scheduled suspension notice, Driver Improvement and Probationary Driver Programs, defensive driving and mature driver courses, violation surcharges, how points are added and removed, moving violation point values, and the two interstate compacts","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driver programs, surcharges and points: DUI with a minor aboard, the scheduled suspension notice, Driver Improvement and Probationary Driver Programs, defensive driving and mature driver courses, violation surcharges, how points are added and removed, moving violation point values, and the two interstate compacts
Knowledge domain: how New Jersey tracks risky drivers through points and surcharges, which programs a driver must or may take to keep or reduce points, how many points common moving violations carry, and how out-of-state tickets follow a New Jersey driver home.

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
A parent or guardian convicted of DUI with a passenger under 18 in the vehicle commits a disorderly persons offense, faces up to six months of suspension and must do up to five days of community service. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver who accumulates 12 to 14 points within a 24-month period receives a Notice of Scheduled Suspension from the MVC by mail. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
After that notice, the driver may attend a New Jersey Driver Improvement Program, ask for a hearing, or surrender the license for the suspension period. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A02
Successfully completing a Driver Improvement Program takes three points off the driver's record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A02
Before scheduling a Driver Improvement or Probationary Driver class with a private provider, the driver pays the MVC a $75 administration fee, plus a separate fee to the provider. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A02
After finishing a Driver Improvement Program or having driving privileges restored, a driver serves a one-year probationary period in which any moving violation leads to a scheduled suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A02
A two-year probationary driver period begins once a driver receives a special learner or examination permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
During that probationary period, two or more moving violations adding up to four or more points require enrollment in the Probationary Driver Program. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
Completing the Probationary Driver Program can cut up to three points, but skipping it or picking up another moving point violation during the test period brings a suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A03
Finishing a voluntary defensive driving course removes two points from the license and may qualify the driver for a lower insurance rate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A03
The MVC credits a defensive driving course toward point reduction only once every five years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A03
Mature drivers aged 55 and older can take defensive driving courses at various driving schools or through specific organizations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A04
A driver with six or more points within three years owes a surcharge of $150 for six points plus $25 for each point above six. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A04
Points count toward surcharges from the date the violation is posted to the record, not the date it happened. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A04
Standard point reductions do not apply to the surcharge system, and a surcharge is paid every year for three years on top of any court fines. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A04
The yearly surcharge is $100 for driving unlicensed and $250 for driving while suspended or for having no liability insurance on a motor vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A04
A DUI or refusal carries a $1,000 yearly surcharge, which rises to $1,500 for a third offense within three years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A05
Unpaid surcharges can lead to collection action, including a Superior Court judgment, a lien on real property or wage garnishment. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A05
Point violations recorded after March 1, 1974, stay on a driver's record permanently. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A05
A traffic violation committed in another state adds two points to a New Jersey record. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A05
Up to three points come off a driver's total for each year without a violation or suspension, but the total never drops below zero. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A06
Racing on a highway carries 5 points, and failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk carries 2 points. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A06
Failing to keep to the right of a vehicle coming from the opposite direction carries 5 points, while passing improperly on the right or off the roadway carries 4. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A07
Tailgating and reckless driving each carry 5 points, while careless driving carries 2. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A07
Speeding 1 to 14 mph over the limit costs 2 points, 15 to 29 mph over costs 4 points, and 30 mph or more over costs 5 points. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A07
Improper passing in a no passing zone carries 4 points. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A07
Using a handheld phone while driving carries 3 points, assessed on a third conviction within 10 years of the second and on every fourth or later offense. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A07
An improper turn at a traffic light, an improper right or left turn and an improper U-turn each carry 3 points. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A08
Improperly passing a school bus carries 5 points, and improperly passing a frozen dessert truck carries 4. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0142]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A08
Leaving the scene of a crash costs 2 points when no one is hurt and 8 points when there is personal injury. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0142]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A08
Violating the Move Over Law, failing to obey Stop or Yield signs and committing a moving violation out of state each carry 2 points. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0142]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A08
Under the Nonresident Violator Compact, a driver ticketed in a member state must satisfy the citation or risk suspension in their home state. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0142]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A08
Under the Driver License Compact, violations from other member states become part of a driver's New Jersey record. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0142]

Misconceptions: points do not vanish once a ticket is paid, they stay on the record and only come off through clean years or approved courses; a defensive driving course cannot be repeated every year for credit; surcharges are separate from court fines and are not reduced by point credits; tickets from other states do follow a New Jersey driver home.
Mnemonics: three points off for Driver Improvement, two off for defensive driving, up to three off per clean year; six points in three years triggers the surcharge; five points for racing, tailgating, reckless driving and passing a school bus; eight points for leaving an injury crash.
Glossary: point system means the MVC record of moving violations weighted by seriousness; violation surcharge means a yearly MVC charge paid for three years; Driver Improvement Program means the course offered after a scheduled suspension notice; Probationary Driver Program means the course required for new drivers with repeat violations; interstate compact means an agreement among states to share violation information.
Dynamic facts: program fees, surcharge amounts, payment channels and the lists of compact member states can change; confirm them on the official MVC website.
